"Use the substitution $u=x^{3} + 1$. Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "c86eaeec-6ebb-5ca2-b873-ed22e534b43c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$"] [:db/add "c86eaeec-6ebb-5ca2-b873-ed22e534b43c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "c86eaeec-6ebb-5ca2-b873-ed22e534b43c" :question/answer-fields $$

$$
